q: What is the minimum age to apply for a New York learner permit?
exp: New York residents may apply for a learner permit at 16.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/get-learner-permit; NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Types of Licenses

q: How many questions are on the New York written permit test taken at a DMV office?
exp: The office written test asks 20 questions.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Vision and Knowledge Tests

q: How many of the 20 permit test questions must you answer correctly to pass?
exp: You need at least 14 correct answers out of 20.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Vision and Knowledge Tests

q: The New York permit test has four road sign questions. How many must you get right?
exp: You must answer at least two of the four sign questions correctly, even if your total score is high enough.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Vision and Knowledge Tests

q: What vision do you need to pass the New York DMV vision test?
d: 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without lenses
exp: The standard is 20/40 vision in at least one eye, and glasses or contacts may be used.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Vision and Knowledge Tests

q: How old must a supervising driver be when a New York learner permit holder practices?
exp: The supervisor must be 21 or older and licensed for the vehicle being driven.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, The Learner Permit; DMV form MV-500H (11/21), Important Information About Learner Permits

q: Before a road test, a New York driver under 18 must certify how much supervised practice?
a: At least 40 hours, including 10 at night
b: At least 60 hours, including 20 at night
c: At least 50 hours, including 15 after sunset
d: At least 30 hours, including 5 at night
exp: A parent or guardian certifies 50 hours of practice, at least 15 of them after sunset, on form MV-262.
src: DMV form MV-262 (3/25), Certification of Supervised Driving

q: How long must a driver under 18 hold a New York junior permit before taking the road test?
exp: A junior permit must be held at least six months, not counting time it was suspended or revoked.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Special Rules for Drivers with Junior Permits and Licenses; dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: A New York junior driver has no parent or instructor along. How many passengers under 21 who are not immediate family may ride along?
exp: Junior permit and junior license holders may carry no more than one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Junior Operator Restrictions; DMV form MV-500H (11/21), Important Information About Learner Permits

q: Where in New York may a Class DJ junior license holder never drive?
b: On any road in Nassau County
d: Anywhere in the five boroughs of New York City
exp: A junior license does not allow driving within New York City under any circumstances.
src: dmv.ny.gov/node/9371 (Graduated License Law and restrictions for drivers under 18)

q: A junior permit holder lives in Suffolk County on Long Island. When may this learner practice driving?
c: At any hour with a parent
exp: On Long Island and in New York City, junior permit holders may not drive from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
src: DMV form MV-500H (11/21), Important Information About Learner Permits

q: Upstate, who may supervise a junior permit holder between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.?
a: A parent, guardian, driver education teacher or driving school instructor
c: No one; night driving is banned upstate
exp: Upstate night practice is limited to these supervisors, who must be 21 or older and properly licensed.
src: DMV form MV-500H (11/21), Important Information About Learner Permits

q: What extra equipment does a car need when a junior permit holder practices in New York City?
a: Dual controls, so the supervisor has a brake
exp: In the five boroughs, junior permit practice must be in a car with dual brakes.
src: DMV form MV-500H (11/21), Important Information About Learner Permits

q: With a junior permit, who may sit in the front seat besides you?
exp: A junior permit holder may have no front seat passenger except the supervising driver.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Driving with a Junior Learner Permit

q: Which of these is off limits to every New York learner permit holder?
b: Any road with a 55 mph limit
c: Bridges and tunnels run by the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority
exp: Learners may not drive on these bridges and tunnels, on streets inside New York City parks, or in DMV road test areas.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, General Rules for All Drivers with Learner Permits

q: Which Westchester County parkway is closed to learner permit holders?
exp: Learners may not drive on the Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River or Taconic State parkways in Westchester.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, General Rules for All Drivers with Learner Permits

q: How long is a classroom 5-hour pre-licensing course certificate (MV-278) valid?
exp: The MV-278 is good for one year from issue and must be valid when you book your road test.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/what-pre-licensing-course-and-how-do-i-find-one

q: Who may take the 5-hour pre-licensing course fully online, at their own pace?
exp: The self-paced online version is for permit holders 18 and older; younger students use a classroom or live virtual class.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/what-pre-licensing-course-and-how-do-i-find-one

q: What does the New York 5-hour pre-licensing course include?
d: Classroom lessons on risk, driving habits and alcohol, with no driving
exp: The course has no hands-on driving and does not prepare you for the road test maneuvers.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/what-pre-licensing-course-and-how-do-i-find-one

q: Which form does a parent or guardian sign to certify a teen's practice hours?
exp: The MV-262 certifies the 50 supervised hours and must be given to the examiner at each road test.
src: DMV form MV-262 (3/25), Certification of Supervised Driving

q: How many practice hours in moderate to heavy traffic does the New York manual recommend?
exp: The manual recommends at least 10 of the practice hours in moderate to heavy traffic.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Preparing for the Road Test

q: How can a 17-year-old with a junior license get a senior Class D license?
a: Complete an approved driver education course and turn in the junior license
d: Drive one year without a ticket
exp: With the Student Certificate of Completion (MV-285) on file, a 17-year-old may trade the junior license for a senior license.
src: dmv.ny.gov/node/9371 (Graduated License Law and restrictions for drivers under 18); NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Driver Education

q: Upstate, a junior license holder wants to drive alone at 10 p.m. When is that allowed?
a: Whenever a friend aged 18 rides along
d: Only straight between home and work or a school course
exp: Upstate, from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. a junior driver may drive alone only directly between home and work or a school course.
src: dmv.ny.gov/node/9371 (Graduated License Law and restrictions for drivers under 18)

q: A junior license holder is convicted of one violation worth 3 or more points. What happens?
a: The license is revoked for a year
b: Two extra hours of practice are required
c: The license is suspended for 60 days
exp: One serious violation, or two other violations, suspends a junior permit or license for 60 days.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Special Rules for Drivers with Junior Permits and Licenses

q: What is the penalty for a junior driver's first conviction for texting or using a hand-held phone?
exp: Junior and probationary drivers lose their license for 120 days for a first phone or texting conviction.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2 and Ch. 8, Using a Cellular or Mobile Telephone

q: How long is the probation period for a driver who passes the road test at 18 or older?
exp: Drivers licensed at 18 or older are on probation for six months.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Probation Period for All Other Newly Licensed Drivers

q: A probationary driver is convicted of speeding. What happens to the license?
a: It is revoked for two years
d: Nothing, if it is the first ticket
exp: Speeding during probation brings a 60-day suspension and a new six-month probation period.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Probation Period for All Other Newly Licensed Drivers

q: After failing a New York road test, how long must you wait to take another?
exp: You must wait at least 14 days before retesting, and your permit stays valid.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: You will drive yourself to the road test site. How old must the licensed driver with you be?
exp: If you drive to the test, the accompanying driver must be over 21 and licensed for the test car.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: Who may ride in the car during a New York road test besides you and the examiner?
a: No one; your accompanying driver waits outside
c: A parent in the back seat
exp: Only the accompanying driver may come in the vehicle, and no other passengers are allowed during the test.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: When are New York road test results posted online?
b: After 6 p.m. on the day of the test
d: At the end of the test, by the examiner
exp: Results appear on the DMV results site after 6 p.m. the same day.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: You move to New York with a valid license from another state. How long do you have to get a New York license?
exp: New residents must get a New York license within 30 days of becoming residents.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/exchange-out-of-state-driver-license; NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Non-Resident and New Resident Drivers

q: Your out-of-state license was issued 3 months ago. What must you do to get a New York license?
a: Wait 3 more months, then exchange it
d: Pass the written and road tests and complete the safe driving course
exp: A license held less than six months cannot simply be exchanged; you test like a new driver.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Non-Resident and New Resident Drivers; dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/exchange-out-of-state-driver-license

q: A new resident holds a license from a country other than Canada. What must this driver do?
a: Exchange the license with a vision test only
c: Pass the vision and written tests, take the 5-hour course and pass a road test
exp: Foreign license holders from outside Canada must pass all tests and complete the course.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/driving-in-new-york-state; NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Non-Resident and New Resident Drivers

q: What happens to a foreign driver license when its holder passes the New York road test?
c: It is handed to the license examiner
d: It is mailed back to the home country
exp: The examiner takes the foreign license; you may ask in writing for DMV to hold it on file.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Non-Resident and New Resident Drivers

q: How many points of proof of name must you show when you apply for a New York permit?
exp: Your name documents must add up to at least six points, and one must show your signature.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Proof of Name

q: How much extra does an Enhanced permit or license cost in New York?
exp: An Enhanced document costs $30 on top of the regular fee.
src: dmv.ny.gov/node/941 (driver license and learner permit fees)

q: Under the Green Light law, what can New York residents 16 and older get regardless of citizenship or lawful status?
b: A standard, non-commercial permit and license
exp: Standard permits and licenses are available regardless of status, and the usual tests still apply.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/driver-licenses-and-green-light-law

q: You fail the New York online permit test. When may you try again?
d: The next day at the earliest
exp: After a failed online test you may resubmit and test again after 6 hours.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/take-the-online-learner-permit-test

q: In how many languages does New York offer the Class D permit test?
exp: The test is offered in English and 19 other languages.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/prepare-for-and-take-your-permit-test

q: In New York, what colors are used on destination signs that show directions and distances?
exp: Destination signs are green with white letters.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs

q: A blue sign with white letters points to what?
a: Services such as rest areas, gas and hospitals
exp: Service signs are blue with white letters or symbols.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs

q: What do orange signs with black letters tell you?
a: People are working on or near the road
c: A park or historic site is ahead
exp: Orange work area signs warn that workers may be on or next to the road.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Work Area Signs

q: What is the lowest work area speed limit New York may post?
exp: A work area speed limit as low as 25 mph may be posted.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Work Area Signs; NY VTL 1180(f)

q: You drive through a work zone where no special speed limit is posted. What does New York law expect?
a: Drive at a reduced speed and obey any flag person
d: Speed up to clear the zone quickly
exp: Even without a work area limit, you must slow down in the work zone and obey flag persons.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Work Area Signs

q: How are the letters on a yield sign colored?
b: Red, on a red and white sign
exp: The yield sign is red and white with red letters.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs

q: When must you come to a full stop at a yield sign?
a: When traffic or pedestrians make it necessary
c: Every time, like a stop sign
d: Never; yield means slow down only
exp: Slow down and stop only if traffic or pedestrians require it.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs

q: What shape and colors do most regulation signs have?
a: White rectangles with black letters or symbols
exp: Regulation signs are normally white rectangles, though a few use other shapes or red.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs

q: A sign shows a symbol inside a red circle with a red slash. What does it mean?
a: The action shown is allowed only at night
d: The action shown is not allowed
exp: A red circle and slash forbids the action or vehicle shown.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Other Regulation Signs

q: What is the usual shape and color of a warning sign?
a: A white rectangle with black letters
d: A yellow diamond with black letters or symbols
exp: Warning signs are normally yellow diamonds.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs

q: A yellow and black plaque showing 30 MPH sits under a curve warning sign. What does it tell you?
a: A lower speed is advised through that area
b: Trucks must slow to 30 mph only
d: The legal limit is now 30 mph everywhere
exp: A recommended speed plaque advises a reduced speed for the hazard; it is not the posted limit.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Warning Signs

q: A flag person in a work zone holds up a STOP paddle facing you. What must you do?
c: Stop and wait until signaled to go
exp: Flag person signals must be obeyed; STOP means stop.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Work Area Signs

q: There is no stop line or crosswalk at a stop sign. Where do you stop?
a: In the middle of the intersection
b: Beside the sign post, wherever it stands
d: At the point nearest the intersection where you can see cross traffic, before entering
exp: Without a line or crosswalk, stop before the intersection where you have a view of traffic on the cross road.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Stop Sign

q: Which sign shape does New York use only for stop signs?
exp: Only the stop sign uses the eight-sided octagon.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Signs; MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 2A.05 and 2B.04

q: A fluorescent yellow-green sign shaped like a house with a pointed roof warns of what?
b: A school zone or school crossing
exp: Among warning signs, the five-sided pentagon in fluorescent yellow-green means a school zone or school crossing.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 2A.05, 7B.01 and 7B.02; core Chapter 2

q: A round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR means what?
exp: The round railroad advance warning sign tells you to slow down, look and listen.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Railroad Crossings

q: A yellow sign shaped like a pennant stands on the left side of the road. What does it mark?
c: The start of a no passing zone
exp: The pennant is reserved for no passing zones and faces drivers on the left side.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sec. 2C.53; core Chapter 2

q: On New York route signs, what does the sign's shape tell you?
a: The speed limit on that road
c: Whether the road is a state, U.S. or Interstate route
d: How far the next exit is
exp: Route sign shapes differ for state, U.S. and Interstate routes.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Route Signs

q: What does an Interstate route marker look like?
b: A white shield with black numbers
exp: Interstate markers are red and blue shields.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sec. 2D.11; core Chapter 2

q: A brown sign most likely points you toward what?
exp: Brown signs guide drivers to parks, recreation and historic sites.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Section 2A.06 and Table 2A-2; core Chapter 2

q: A school sign has a small plaque with an arrow pointing down at an angle. What does it mark?
c: The end of the school zone
exp: The downward arrow plaque marks the school crossing location itself.
src: MUTCD 11th ed., Sections 7B.02 and 7B.03; core Chapter 2

q: A lane use sign shows a curved arrow with the word ONLY. What does it require?
a: Only buses may use that lane
b: Turning from that lane is optional
c: Vehicles in that lane must turn the way shown
d: You may not change lanes anywhere
exp: ONLY under an arrow means drivers in that lane must go in that direction.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Pavement Markings (Arrows); MUTCD 11th ed., Sec. 2B.28; core Chapter 2

q: When do posted school speed limits apply in New York?
c: Every day of the year from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.
d: On school days during the posted hours or when the beacons flash
exp: School speed limits apply on school days at the times on the sign, which fall between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m., or while the beacons flash.
src: NY VTL 1180(c)

q: May you make a U-turn in a New York school zone?
a: Yes, if no children are present
exp: New York prohibits U-turns in school zones.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, U-Turns

q: How many points does a conviction for speeding in a New York work zone add?
exp: Speeding in a construction zone now carries 8 points.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: When are speeding fines in New York work zones doubled?
b: Whenever you speed in the zone, even if no workers are present
exp: Work zone speeding fines double even when no workers or work vehicles are there.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, How to Drive Safely in Work Zones; NY VTL 1180(f) and subdivision 3

q: Outside New York City, when may you turn right on a steady red light?
b: After a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign forbids it
c: Without stopping, if the way is clear
d: Only when a green arrow is lit
exp: Right on red is allowed after a full stop unless a sign, signal or marking prohibits it.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Traffic Lights

q: What is the rule for turning on a red light in New York City?
a: Right turns on red are always allowed
b: Turns on red are allowed only at night
c: No turn on red unless a sign allows it
d: Left turns on red are always allowed
exp: In New York City you may not turn on red unless a sign permits it.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Traffic Lights

q: When may you turn left on a steady red light in New York?
a: From a one-way road onto another one-way road, after a full stop
b: From any road onto a two-way road
exp: A left on red is legal only from a one-way road into another one-way road, after stopping and yielding.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Traffic Lights

q: You face a red arrow pointing right. May you turn right after stopping?
a: Yes, but only from the left lane
b: Yes, if no sign forbids it
c: No; New York allows no turn on a red arrow
exp: A right or left turn on red is not permitted at a red arrow.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Traffic Lights

q: Which driver may never turn right on a red light in New York?
c: A driver with a junior license
d: A school bus driver with students aboard
exp: A school bus carrying students may not turn right on any red light.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Traffic Lights

q: On a multi-lane New York interstate, a police car is stopped on the shoulder with lights flashing. What must you do?
c: Move out of the lane next to it if you safely can, and take care
exp: On controlled-access highways and parkways, drivers must move from the adjacent lane when it is safe.
src: NY VTL 1144-a; NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Move Over Law

q: New York's Move Over law covers which of these vehicles?
a: A tow truck stopped with amber lights flashing
b: A car stopped at a red light
c: A bus at a bus stop
d: A parked delivery van on a city street
exp: Hazard vehicles showing amber lights, such as tow trucks and snowplows, are covered.
src: NY VTL 1144-a

q: On a two-lane country road, a fire truck is stopped on the shoulder with lights on. What does the Move Over law require?
a: Nothing, because the road has only two lanes
b: Exercise due care and slow down as you pass
c: Use your horn as you pass
exp: On every road you must take care to avoid the stopped vehicle; changing lanes is required on multi-lane controlled-access roads.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Move Over Law; NY VTL 1144-a

q: On a New York parkway, a car with no flashing lights is stopped on the shoulder. Does the Move Over law apply?
b: Yes, on parkways and controlled-access highways it covers any stopped vehicle
d: No, only vehicles with amber lights count
exp: The law extends to any motor vehicle stopped on a parkway or controlled-access highway.
src: NY VTL 1144-a(d); NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Move Over Law

q: A volunteer firefighter's car shows a flashing blue light. What does New York law say?
b: You must stop as for an ambulance
d: It is not an authorized emergency vehicle, but you should yield as a courtesy and move over when it is stopped
exp: Blue and green lights mark volunteers' personal cars; yield as a courtesy, and the Move Over law covers them when stopped.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Blue, Green and Amber Lights

q: A school bus is stopped on the other side of a divided highway with red lights flashing. What must you do in New York?
a: Stop only if children are visible
exp: In New York you must stop for a school bus even on the opposite side of a divided highway.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 6, School Buses

q: How far from a stopped school bus with flashing red lights does the New York manual say to stop?
exp: The manual advises stopping at least 20 feet from the bus.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 6, School Buses

q: When may you drive on after stopping for a New York school bus?
a: When the bus moves again, or its driver or a police officer signals you on
c: As soon as the children reach the sidewalk
d: When the red lights switch to yellow
exp: Stay stopped until the bus starts moving or you are waved on by the bus driver or an officer.
src: NY VTL 1174(a); NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 6, School Buses

q: What is the fine range for a first conviction for passing a stopped school bus in New York?
exp: A first offense carries a fine of $250 to $400, up to 30 days in jail, or both.
src: NY VTL 1174(c)

q: How many points does passing a stopped school bus add to a New York driving record?
exp: Passing a stopped school bus now carries 8 points.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: What happens after three convictions for passing a stopped school bus within three years?
d: The license is revoked for at least six months
exp: Three school bus passing violations in three years bring a revocation of at least six months.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Speeding and Other Violations; Ch. 6, School Buses

q: From which part of the road must you start a U-turn in New York?
d: The left part of the lane nearest the center line
exp: Make a U-turn from the left portion of the lane closest to the center line, never from the right lane.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, U-Turns

q: Other drivers cannot see your car from how far away if a U-turn is illegal there?
exp: No U-turn where drivers cannot see you from 500 feet away, such as near a hilltop or curve.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, U-Turns

q: Where are U-turns illegal in New York City even without a sign?
exp: U-turns are not allowed in New York City business districts.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, U-Turns

q: On a limited access expressway you see a paved path across the median. May you use it for a U-turn?
exp: U-turns are never allowed on a limited access expressway, even where paths connect the two sides.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, U-Turns

q: May you make a U-turn on a green left turn arrow in New York?
d: Yes, unless a sign prohibits it, yielding to other traffic
exp: A green left arrow allows a U-turn where it is permitted, as long as you yield.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, U-Turns

q: How far ahead does New York law require you to signal a turn?
exp: Signal at least 100 feet before turning, with your turn lights or hand signals.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Turns

q: How far before a lane change must you signal in New York?
b: No signal is needed on highways
exp: The same 100-foot rule applies to lane changes.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 6, How to Pass

q: How far before an expressway exit ramp should you signal?
exp: Signal your exit at least 100 feet before the ramp.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Expressway Driving

q: What is the speed limit in New York when no limit is posted, outside New York City?
exp: If no limit is posted, drive no faster than 55 mph.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Speed

q: What is the speed limit in New York City unless another limit is posted?
exp: New York City's default limit is 25 mph.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Speed

q: What is the highest speed limit that may be posted on some New York rural expressways?
exp: Expressway limits are normally 55 mph but may be posted at 65 mph in some rural areas.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Expressway Driving

q: How many points does New York charge for driving 11 to 20 mph over the limit?
exp: Speeding 11 to 20 mph over the limit is worth 4 points.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: How many points does New York charge for driving more than 40 mph over the limit?
exp: Speeding more than 40 mph over the limit is worth 11 points, enough on its own to trigger a suspension.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: How many points within 24 months can lead to a New York license suspension?
exp: Collecting 11 points in 24 months can bring a suspension.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: What following distance does the New York manual teach in good conditions?
exp: Use the two-second rule, counting from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Allow Yourself Space

q: How should you change your following distance in bad weather or behind a large truck?
c: Shorten it to stay in the truck's draft
d: Increase it to at least three or four seconds
exp: The manual says to increase the count to at least three or four seconds.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Allow Yourself Space

q: How many points does a following too closely (tailgating) conviction add in New York?
exp: Following too closely is worth 4 points.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: What pavement symbol marks a New York lane reserved for buses, carpools or other special vehicles?
exp: The diamond symbol marks reserved lanes such as bus and HOV lanes.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Pavement Markings (Diamond Symbol)

q: When may a car that does not meet the occupancy rule use an HOV lane?
b: When the signs show the restriction is not in effect
c: Any time it stays under the speed limit
exp: Follow the occupancy rules for the hours posted on the signs.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Pavement Markings (Diamond Symbol)

q: On a city street, the line beside a diamond lane becomes a broken white line near a corner. What may you do there?
b: Pass slower traffic in the lane
d: Enter the lane to turn right at the next intersection
exp: Where the line is broken, other drivers may enter the reserved lane to make a right turn at the next intersection.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 4, Pavement Markings (Diamond Symbol)

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in New York?
exp: You may not park within 15 feet of a hydrant unless a licensed driver stays in the car.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, Parking Regulations

q: In New York, you may not park or stand within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
exp: Parking or standing within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection is not allowed.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, Parking Regulations

q: How close may you park to a traffic light, stop sign or yield sign in New York?
exp: Parking or standing within 30 feet of these is not allowed.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, Parking Regulations

q: How far from a railroad crossing must you park in New York?
exp: You cannot park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, Parking Regulations

q: Across the street from a fire station driveway, how far away must you park in New York?
exp: The rule is 20 feet on the station's side and 75 feet on the opposite side.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, Parking Regulations

q: After parallel parking in New York, how close to the curb must your wheels be?
exp: In your final position your wheels must be no more than one foot from the curb.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, How to Park

q: What may you do at a New York NO PARKING sign?
a: Stop briefly to load or unload passengers or merchandise
b: Nothing; you may not stop at all
c: Leave the car for up to an hour
exp: No Parking still allows a temporary stop to load or unload.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 7, Parking Regulations

q: How much space must you leave when passing a bicycle in New York?
b: A safe distance on its left until you are clear; the law sets no number of feet
exp: New York law requires passing on the left at a safe distance until clear of the bicycle.
src: NY VTL 1122-a; NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Turns

q: Which bicycle riders and passengers must wear a helmet in New York?
exp: State law requires helmets for bicycle riders and passengers aged 1 to 13.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 11, Bicyclists

q: A bicycle is riding in the lane inside a roundabout ahead of you. What should you do?
c: Stay behind it and do not pass
d: Pass it once you are halfway around
exp: Bicyclists ride in the roundabout lane like other vehicles; do not pass them there.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Roundabouts

q: Why should you slow down as you pass a bicyclist?
a: The air pushed by a fast vehicle can throw the rider off balance
b: Bicycles have the right of way in every lane
c: Bicycles always turn left without warning
d: It is required only at night
exp: Air pressure from a passing vehicle can unbalance a rider.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 11, Bicyclists

q: Above what property damage amount must a New York crash be reported to DMV?
exp: Report any crash with $1,000 or more damage to one person's property, or any injury or death.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 12, Reports to DMV

q: Within how many days must you file a crash report (MV-104) with New York DMV?
exp: The report is due to DMV within 10 days, even if you told your insurer.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 12, Reports to DMV

q: What is failing to file a required crash report in New York?
b: A misdemeanor that can cost you your license
d: No offense if your insurer knows
exp: Not reporting is a criminal offense and can lead to suspension or revocation.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 12, Reports to DMV

q: The driver is injured and cannot fill out the crash report. Who may do it?
a: A passenger or the vehicle owner
exp: A passenger or the owner may complete the report for an injured driver.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 12, Reports to DMV

q: You hit a parked car and cannot find its owner. What does New York law require?
b: Wait at the car for 24 hours
c: Report it to the nearest police station as soon as you can
exp: If the owner is not present, report the incident to police as soon as physically able.
src: NY VTL 600(1)(a)

q: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle must you switch to low beams in New York?
exp: Use low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Night Driving

q: Within what distance of a vehicle you are following must you use low beams in New York?
exp: Use low beams within 200 feet of a vehicle ahead, even one in another lane.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Night Driving

q: When does New York law require headlights?
b: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and whenever wipers are needed
exp: Headlights are also required when visibility is under 1,000 feet.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Night Driving

q: Visibility drops below what distance before New York requires your headlights?
exp: Turn on headlights whenever you can see less than 1,000 feet ahead.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Night Driving

q: In New York, a BAC of more than 0.05 but below 0.08 is legal evidence of what?
exp: A BAC over 0.05 is evidence of impairment; 0.08 or higher is evidence of intoxication.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and the Law

q: At what BAC can a New York driver be charged with aggravated DWI?
exp: A BAC of 0.18 or more is evidence of aggravated driving while intoxicated.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Alcohol, Other Drugs, and the Law

q: Under New York's zero tolerance law, what BAC range applies to drivers under 21?
exp: Drivers under 21 with a BAC from 0.02 to 0.07 violate the zero tolerance law.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Zero Tolerance

q: What happens after a first zero tolerance finding for a driver under 21?
d: A six-month suspension, a $125 civil penalty and a $100 fee
exp: The license is suspended six months; getting it back costs a $125 civil penalty and a $100 termination fee.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Zero Tolerance; Ch. 2, Fees and Civil Penalties

q: A driver 21 or older refuses a chemical test after an arrest for the first time. What is the minimum revocation?
exp: A first refusal brings a revocation of at least one year and a $500 civil penalty.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Chemical Test Refusals

q: When is a license first suspended after a New York chemical test refusal?
a: Never; refusal has no license penalty
d: At arraignment in court on the alcohol or drug charge
exp: The license is suspended at arraignment, and revoked if a DMV hearing confirms the refusal.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Chemical Tests

q: What civil penalty must be paid to DMV after a chemical test refusal revocation?
exp: A refusal revocation carries a $500 civil penalty, or $750 within five years of a prior offense.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Fees and Civil Penalties

q: What is the fine range for a first DWI conviction in New York?
exp: A first DWI is a misdemeanor with a $500 to $1,000 fine, up to a year in jail and at least a six-month revocation.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Penalties for Alcohol/Drug Related Violations

q: What license penalty follows a first DWAI (alcohol) conviction in New York?
exp: A first DWAI brings a 90-day suspension and a $300 to $500 fine.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Penalties for Alcohol/Drug Related Violations

q: Under Leandra's Law, driving while intoxicated with a child under 16 in the car can be charged as what?
exp: It can be charged as a class E felony, punishable by up to four years in prison.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, The Ignition Interlock Program and Leandra's Law

q: Who may have an open container of alcohol in a car on a New York road?
a: No driver, and no passenger except in vehicles such as licensed limousines
b: Anyone, if the car is moving slowly
c: The driver, if it stays closed in the cup holder
exp: Drinking or holding an open alcohol container in the vehicle is an infraction for drivers and passengers.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 9, Open Container Law

q: How many points does a hand-held phone or texting violation add in New York?
exp: Any mobile phone or portable electronic device violation is worth 5 points.
src: dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; DMV news release on point values effective 2026-02-16

q: What is the maximum fine for a first texting while driving offense in New York?
exp: A first offense carries a fine of up to $200; it rises to $250 and $450 for repeat offenses within 18 months.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Penalties for Texting, Electronic Device Use

q: Which phone use is legal for a fully licensed adult driver in New York?
a: Reading a text on the highway
b: Typing an email at low speed
d: Holding the phone to your ear
exp: A hands-free phone that needs neither hand may be used at any time.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Using a Cellular or Mobile Telephone

q: A third texting offense within 18 months can bring a fine of up to how much in New York?
exp: A third or later offense within 18 months has a fine of up to $450.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Penalties for Texting, Electronic Device Use

q: Which passengers must wear a seat belt in New York?
c: Every passenger 16 or older, in any seat, plus younger children in belts or child seats
exp: Drivers and passengers 16 and older must buckle up; younger passengers must be in a belt or child restraint.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

q: A 12-year-old passenger is not buckled up. Who gets the ticket in New York?
d: No one; belts are optional under 16
exp: The driver is responsible for passengers under 16 and faces a fine and 3 points.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

q: Can New York police stop you just because someone in your car is not wearing a seat belt?
b: Yes, it is a primary enforcement state
exp: New York is a primary enforcement state for seat belts.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

q: Until what age must a New York child ride rear-facing, unless the seat's limits are outgrown?
exp: Children ride rear-facing until age 2 or until they reach the seat maker's height or weight limit.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

q: What restraint does New York require for a child aged 4 to 7?
b: No restraint in the back seat
c: A booster seat or other child restraint used with a lap and shoulder belt
exp: Children 4 to 7 need an approved child restraint, commonly a booster, used with a lap and shoulder belt.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

q: A 6-year-old is 4 feet 10 inches tall. What may this child use in New York?
a: A seat belt, because the child is over 4 feet 9 inches
d: Must stay in a rear-facing seat
exp: A child 4 to 7 who is over 4 feet 9 inches or over 100 pounds may use a seat belt.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 8, Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags

q: What is New York's minimum liability coverage for injury to one person?
exp: Minimums are $25,000/$50,000 for injury, $50,000/$100,000 for death and $10,000 for property damage.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 3, Insurance

q: Your car insurance is about to end and you will not renew it. What should you do?
a: Keep driving until the registration expires
b: Turn in the plates at a motor vehicle office before coverage ends
d: Remove the plates and keep them
exp: Return the plates first; 90 uninsured days without returning them suspends your license.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 3, Insurance

q: How often must most New York vehicles pass a safety inspection?
exp: After the first inspection, a vehicle must be reinspected before its current certificate expires, which is annual.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 3, Inspection

q: Within how many days must you tell New York DMV about a change of address?
exp: Notify DMV within 10 days, by mail or online.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 1, Change of Address

q: Which of these is scored on the New York road test?
c: Parallel parking and a three-point turn
exp: Parking, backing and the three-point turn are one of the scored groups.
src: dmv.ny.gov/dmv/scoring-summary-electronic-notification

q: Which car feature may you not use during a New York road test?
exp: Certain safety features, such as parking assist and cruise control, are not allowed during the test.
src: NY Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 13, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems

q: Leaving the curb on the New York road test, which error is scored?
a: Using only the mirror and not checking the blind spot
c: Starting the engine with the brake pressed
exp: Failing to observe, failing to signal and relying on the mirror alone are scored when leaving the curb.
src: dmv.ny.gov/dmv/scoring-summary-electronic-notification

q: What must a driver under 18 give the examiner at every New York road test?
b: A letter from a driving school
c: A practice log from an app
d: A completed Certification of Supervised Driving (MV-262)
exp: The MV-262 is required each time a driver under 18 takes the road test.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: What happens to your learner permit if you fail the New York road test?
a: It stays valid until its expiration date
exp: A failed test does not affect your permit.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: When do extra road test fees apply in New York?
d: After you fail your first two road tests
exp: You pay additional fees once your first two road tests have been used and failed.
src: dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test

q: In New York, an ambulance with red lights flashing comes toward you in the opposite lane of a two-lane road. What must you do?
a: Keep going, since it is in the other lane
b: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop
c: Stop where you are in your lane
d: Speed up to clear the area
exp: You must pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle from any direction, even one in the opposite lane of a two-way road.
src: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 5, Emergency Vehicles; VTL 1144(a)

q: On a New York one-way road with three lanes, a fire truck with its lights and siren on comes up behind you. Where may you pull over?
c: To either edge of the road
exp: New York law lets drivers on a one-way roadway three or more lanes wide pull to either edge, clear of any intersection.
src: VTL 1144(a)

q: How close may you follow a New York fire truck that has its emergency lights on?
exp: Drivers not on official business may not follow a fire vehicle with its lights on closer than 200 feet.
src: VTL 1217

q: Do daytime running lights meet New York's headlight rule when your wipers are on?
a: No, you must turn on your headlights
b: Yes, they always count as headlights
exp: New York requires headlights when weather calls for wipers, and daytime running lights do not qualify as headlights.
src: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Night Driving; Driving in Rain, Fog, or Snow

q: It is midday and you turn on your wipers to clear sleet. What does New York law require?
exp: New York law requires headlights whenever you use your wipers to clear rain, snow, sleet or fog.
src: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 10, Night Driving; Driving in Rain, Fog, or Snow

q: At a New York traffic stop, you cannot show the officer a driver license. How does the law treat this?
a: As evidence that you are not licensed
b: As no problem, because police can look it up
exp: Failure to show a valid license to a police officer is presumptive evidence that the driver is not licensed.

q: May you show a photocopy of your registration certificate to a New York police officer?
c: Only if the car is less than one year old
d: Only with an insurance card attached
exp: New York law lets the operator produce a photostatic copy of the registration certificate instead of the original.

q: At a New York traffic stop, what does the law require when an officer gives you a lawful order?
a: You may ignore it if you think the stop is unfair
b: You must follow it only if it is in writing
d: You must comply only after calling a lawyer
exp: No person may fail or refuse to comply with any lawful order or direction of a police officer.
src: VTL 1102

q: A 19-year-old uses a driver license to lie about their age and buy beer in New York. What can the court do to the license the first time?
exp: If a driver license was used for an illegal alcohol purchase, the court can suspend the license for three months for a first violation.
src: ABC Law 65-b(6)(a)

q: In New York, a person under 21 found holding alcohol to drink it can be fined up to:
exp: Possession with intent to consume under 21 brings a fine of up to $50, community service up to 30 hours or an alcohol awareness program.
src: ABC Law 65-c

q: A New York driver under 21 uses a driver license to buy alcohol illegally for the second time. How long is the license suspended?
b: One year or until age 21, whichever is longer
exp: If a driver license was used, a second violation brings a six-month suspension; a third or later brings one year or until age 21, whichever is longer.
src: ABC Law 65-b(6)(b), (c)

q: How long do points count toward a New York license suspension?
c: 24 months from the date of the violation
exp: Points are counted from the date of the violation and stop counting once 24 months have passed.
src: https://dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system

q: How many points can a DMV-approved crash prevention course subtract when New York DMV counts toward a suspension?
exp: Completing the course subtracts up to 4 points when DMV calculates a suspension; it also cuts insurance premiums up to 10 percent.
src: https://dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2

q: How many points within 18 months bring a New York Driver Responsibility Assessment?
exp: Six or more points in 18 months bring a yearly Driver Responsibility Assessment for three years.
src: https://dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system; New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21), Ch. 2, Driver Responsibility Assessments

q: How many points does any alcohol- or drug-related driving conviction add in New York?
exp: Since the updated point values, any alcohol- or drug-related conviction or incident carries 11 points.
src: https://dmv.ny.gov/news/dmv-reminds-new-yorkers-of-updated-point-values-for-driving-violations

q: How many points does running a red light or a STOP sign add in New York?
exp: Violating a traffic signal, STOP sign or YIELD sign carries 3 points.
src: https://dmv.ny.gov/points-and-penalties/the-new-york-state-driver-point-system

q: After failing a New York road test, how long must you wait before you can retest?
exp: After a failed road test, you must wait 14 days before you can take it again.
src: https://dmv.ny.gov/driver-license/schedule-and-take-road-test
